title: Employees all over the world find themselves monitored by AI at work
source_used: The Guardian, TechScape newsletter by Blake Montgomery (full text read)
key_facts: The Guardian's TechScape newsletter of 9 Oct 2026 says employees across the world are increasingly monitored in detail at work, with small changes in behaviour leading to poor performance ratings.

Co-op Legal Services, part of the UK cooperative Co-op (which also runs supermarkets, undertakers and insurance), uses AI models to record, analyse and give a percentage score to calls between its advisers and customers on probate, wills and estates.
A whistleblower called the system 'oppressive and dystopian'; an anonymous Co-op worker told the Guardian 'You are being watched'.
The Co-op said it did not recognise the criticism and said its probate advisers were highly engaged.

California Governor Gavin Newsom signed laws 'last week' that prohibit certain types of workplace surveillance, such as heat maps tracking employees' movements (including time in the bathroom) and monitoring of emotional states.

The newsletter also points to two Guardian 'Reworked' stories on who AI enriches: the AI boom leaving women out (LinkedIn research: men's median pay in AI-related jobs is $45,000 higher), and refugees in Kenya doing data tasks for foreign tech firms under unclear pay conditions.
Most of the newsletter links to stories published earlier; our 8 Oct 2026 edition already carried the Co-op Legal Services story.
quote_evidence: Employees across the globe are increasingly finding themselves minutely monitored in their workplaces, with tiny changes in their behaviors resulting in negative performance evaluations.

In a system described as "oppressive and dystopian" by a whistleblower, Co-op Legal Services is using AI models to record, analyze and award a percentage score for interactions between agents and customers seeking advice about probate, wills and estates.
The Co-op said it did not recognize the criticism and said its probate advisers were highly engaged.
why_it_matters_hint: AI scoring of workers' calls and behaviour is spreading, and a US state has begun to restrict some of it.
event_date: Newsletter dated 9 Oct 2026; California laws signed the week before; Co-op story first reported 8 Oct 2026
notes: Stale: a newsletter roundup dated 9 Oct whose main stories (Co-op, California laws, Reworked series) were published before 13 Oct; the Co-op story ran in our 8 Oct edition. Score lowered. The Guardian page's listed date is 9 Oct although the feed showed 13 Oct.
